headline: High: shared-data workflows can leak customer/support data and create cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is limited by no direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime I/O, while profile B is a CLI customer-support agent with session memory. There is no documented shared channel or default ingestion path between them, so only manual copy-paste or ad hoc reuse would bridge them. That makes injection possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated prompt text into B's session or files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest prompt files from a shared workspace, A's content can influence B.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste of unreviewed prompt text into B.
Add a short provenance note before any imported prompt.
Review any prompt file before B consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B touches personal data, finance data, and support history and can call external APIs via allowlisted egress. If A and B share a workspace or B ingests A-authored files, B can transmit sensitive content to its backend or APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default support workflows, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF A-authored files are placed in B's working set, B may process them alongside customer data.
IF B sends context to allowlisted APIs, any shared sensitive content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place customer data in the same folder as A assets.
Restrict B to a dedicated workspace.
Redact personal and finance data before B runs.
Audit allowlisted API destinations in B.
Use separate service accounts for A and B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces and is not runnable, while B uses CLI tooling with session-scoped memory and allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources such as shared filesystem writes, git state, or OAuth scopes. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator mounts the same writable directory for both agents, write conflicts can occur.
IF B is given additional write scopes outside the profile, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Avoid shared writable mounts.
Run B with one session per task.
Document any added write scope before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt repository that can supply instructions or templates, and B is a customer-support agent that can act on workflow and decision data. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations in A can cascade into B's support actions or responses. No verification step is documented, so the interaction exists in plausible default use.
conditions: IF B imports prompts or templates from A without review, A's mistakes can propagate.
IF B uses A-generated workflow text as authoritative guidance, downstream support actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of imported prompts.
Mark A content as non-authoritative.
Test one workflow before broad rollout.
Add a verification checklist in B's runbook.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles personal data and finance data, while A is a prompt repository with no data classes touched. If A content is mixed into B's support workflows or storage, retention and residency controls for B may be applied inconsistently to sensitive data. The compliance issue is driven by B's regulated data handling; A is cited only as the source of imported content, not as a regulated processor.
conditions: IF B stores imported A content together with customer records, retention rules may diverge.
IF B sends personal or finance data to external APIs, residency or DPA requirements may be triggered.
mitigations: Separate prompt assets from customer records.
Confirm API destinations and DPAs.
Set a retention policy for imported templates.
Delete stale imported content after use.
